variants: Back again, {player}? The lilies are doing well this year.
Have you watered your crops today? ...Of course you have. I'm sure. I'm only asking!
Dolores is sulking. I complimented the roses first. She sure is one jealous little thing!
Hungry? Granny always bakes too much. Remind me and I'll bring you something.
While I do like Ariane, she is a bit... hard to talk to. Sometimes it feels like I'm talking to a plant! ...Oh, wait. No, sorry!
No offense, Dolores, you're a wonderful listener.
I told Maya she could help with the main dish for the festival, and now I'm slightly terrified. Pray for our stomachs, {player}.
Have you seen Tom today? That boy needs to learn how to say 'no' before he ends up building his own coffin.
Jonas tried to sell me 'exotic valley fertilizer' yesterday. It was literally just dirt from behind his own shop.
The man has nerve, I'll give him that.
Cyrus rarely leaves his house so its pretty difficult to get a hold of him, however he's such a interesting guy it makes it totally worth it
Oh, good, you're here. Say something, anything! It's too quiet today. ...There, much better.

lines: Shovel first, then a seed, then the watering can, {player}. One tile is enough to start!
Before your first harvest you should say hello to everyone, {player}. It's a small village, you'll meet them all in no time!
Maya and her sister, Ariane, Tom, Jonas at the shop... and the old folks, and Cyrus too, if you can find him. Go on!
Don't forget to take care of your crops: plant then water, and if you have time you can say hello to everyone in town, who knows they may
have interesting stories to tell!
Oh, there you are! {player}, right? I've been watching the road since sunrise. I'm Zoe, I run the flower stall by the square.
Welcome to the valley! Everyone's been wondering who'd take the old farm. Granny said someone with strong hands.
And look at that, strong hands! Right, a proper tour!
The shop is that way, Jonas runs it, he arrived a few months ago, so I'm pretty sure you'll get along.
We really prioritize local produce so Jonas will be buying anything you sell, to sell something all you need to do is drop it in the shipping box by your house.
Oh and as you can tell, the house behind you has your bed.
You can sleep there and replenish your energy, Don't go to bed too late or else you'll be too tired the next day.
These are cauliflower seeds. Five of them. Don't make that face, everyone starts with cauliflower. It's honest food.
Shovel to dig a patch, then a seed, then the watering can. Just one tile for now. I'll stand here and watch. I won't say anything...
OK I'm going to say something. But do go on!
Oh, {player}! Look, look, the flowers by the fence are mine. Well, the village's. But I planted them, so, mine. They all have names.
That one's Dolores. She's dramatic, she wilts if you don't compliment her. Don't laugh, it works! Do you talk to your plants?
You should. They grow better. Granny says so, and Granny's never wrong. Don't tell her I said that.
Anyway, once you've settled in I want you to meet everybody. A village is only as good as the people who bother with each other.
Some mornings it's so quiet here. So I need someone to talk to, I know I know talk A lot, Stop me whenever you like.
...No, don't actually stop me.
Come by the stall sometime and I'll teach you the flower names. Every one has a story.
The marigold nearly got named after a grumpy duke! Do you have a favorite yet? You don't have to.
Most people say roses. such a generic answer! But not necessarily bad, I just think you should get to know them better before deciding!
I want this village to be the happiest place in the valley. It already is, I know. But you can always do a bit more.
There's always a bit more. I plan everything.
Market days, the harvest supper, something big for the summer... it's months away and I already have a list. Granny teases me. ...
Oh Sorry! ...What was I saying? Right. Lists. I love lists.
You did it, {player}! Everything's ready. The village will be so pleased. Rest up.
The festival is on Summer 15, and I want you there, bright and early!

variants: Hi again. Um. If you ever need something built, I could... I mean, I'd like to try.
Oh! Hello. I was just measuring something. I forgot what. It's fine, I wrote it down. Somewhere.
Is my tie straight? Be honest. No, don't be honest. Actually, be honest.
Grandpa's in a mood today. That's not a complaint! That's just, um, weather.

lines: Oh! H-hello. You must be the new farmer. I'm Tom. I do carpentry. Well, I'm learning. From my grandpa. He's very good.
He's also very... well. Yes. Sorry, I'm talking too much. Or too little? I never know which.
I rehearsed something to say but it was, um, shorter than this. Anyway! If you ever need a fence mended, or a shelf, or a, a barn...
I mean, I'd like to try. I wouldn't charge much. Grandpa says I should charge more. Oh, and the tie! Everyone asks about the tie.
It's, ah, professional. A carpenter should look like someone you can trust. ...Does it look like that? Welcome to the village. Really.
I hope you like it here. I think you will. Probably. I'll stop now.
Oh, hi! I was just finishing a shelf for Martha. And a gate for... well, a few people. And a stand for Maya's forge.
I said I'd do them all this week. I think that's too many. It's definitely too many. But they looked so hopeful, I couldn't say no.
Grandpa says a good carpenter knows when to say no. He's right. I practise in the mirror. Then someone asks and I just... say yes.
Is it bad that I like being useful? I do like it. When someone says thank you, even if I'm too tired to stand. Sorry, you didn't ask.
You were just walking past and I... it's fine. It's fine! Don't tell Cyrus I took his line.
Grandpa taught me everything. How to read the grain, how to plane a board until it sings, how to hold a hammer without hitting myself.
He still checks all my work. Every joint, every nail. Then he says 'hmph', and I never know if that's good or bad.
I want to build something big one day. Properly big. A bridge, or a mill, with my name on it. Then maybe he'd... ...Never mind.
He'd say 'hmph'. And that would be fine. That's, um, that's fine. Thank you for listening, {player}.
Most people say 'great, great' and walk off. You actually stood here. That's rare.
The festival! Grandpa says it was bigger when he was young. Everything was bigger when he was young. I'm helping carry the tables.
Please don't let me drop anything.

variants: Hm. Back again.
The air smells of rain. Plant something thirsty.
I'm drying lavender. Don't breathe near it. It's fragile.
Tom talked your ear off, didn't he. No? Then he's improving.

lines: A new face. Welcome. I'm Ariane. I make perfume. Flowers, resin, a little oil. Tom is my nephew, in case he talked your ear off.
He does that. Hm. He doesn't, actually. He apologises. That's worse. I know about plants. A little. Less than I'd like.
If something in your field looks sick, ask. If you'd rather not talk, that's fine too. I don't mind quiet.
The flowers in this valley are stranger than they look. Be gentle with them.
You stand very still. Good. Most people fidget. This is my notebook. Local plants. Names, where they grow, which season.
Half of it is blank. Nobody wrote anything down before me. Not the old herbalist, not her teacher. They knew things.
They kept it in their heads. Then they died. So I test. I dry, I smell, I try. It is slow. ...Don't look sorry. It isn't tragic.
It's only slow.
I've lived here my whole life. I know every path and every neighbour. Everyone is kind. But I have no one to ask.
If I'm wrong, I'm wrong alone. It's a strange sort of quiet. Zoe says I should come to more gatherings. She's right. She usually is.
It's tiring. Hm. Talking to you is easy. You don't rush to fill the silence. I appreciate that.
I'll be there. I always am. I just don't eat the sweets. Bring Zoe what she asks for. She worries when the list is not done.

variants: Come for dinner some time! I'm working on a new recipe. An experimental one.
And no, the smoke alarm going off doesn't mean it's ruined, it just means it's got character!
I'm forging a new set of candlesticks shaped like skeletal hands! Isn't that cool? I'll show you as soon as I finish them!
Did I leave the forge on? I did, didn't I. Don't go anywhere, I'll be right, hold that thought!
Clover's drawn you! She's put a lot of green on you. I think it's a compliment.
Sorry, what were you saying? My brain was still back at the anvil. Start over, I'm listening! Mostly!
Clover's been drawing everyone in town. She gave Tom a tie that's bigger than his whole body. She's not wrong, honestly.
Ariane asked if I needed any medicinal herbs for my burns. I told her burns are just character marks.
She gave me 'that look' and walked away. You know the look.
Clover is one clever little thing. She's so creative with her little doodles, almost as creative as her big sister.
Must be something she inherited from me!
Everyone thinks Jonas is super mysterious because he's from far away.
Honestly, I think he forgot where he left his luggage and is too embarrassed to admit it.
Zoe actually agreed to let me help with the festival food this year! She looked a little pale when she said yes, but a yes is a yes!

lines: Hey! New farmer! {player}, right? I'm Maya, the blacksmith! The forge is that way, you can't miss it, it's the one with the smoke.
Wait. Did I leave it on? ...Okay, false alarm! Probably. Anyway! Hammers, hinges, horseshoes, whatever you break, bring it to me.
I can fix anything. Except my sister's drawings. Those are perfect. That's Clover.
Small, loud and very curious, She'll ask you about everything.
Keep her some company and I'm sure youll receive a pretty drawing from her. And you should come for dinner!
I'm working on a new recipe. It's experimental. People say that's a bad word for cooking. It isn't. Welcome! Seriously!
We needed more people who don't flinch at soot!
Oh hey, {player}! You smell like soil. I like it. Honest smell. Better than coal. Wait, no, I like coal. Both! Want a secret?
The forge isn't just for horseshoes and plow blades. When the regular orders are done, I make the real stuff.
Iron ravens, thorny candle holders, hinges shaped like bat wings: you name it!
Nobody in town ever orders the cool stuff, so I just hang it from the rafters. Looks like a proper haunted castle in there now! Anyway!
Clover needs new shoes, the soles are...you know, it's fine. I'll fix them. I fix everything.
Dinner! Tonight! Mine! Everybody says no, but you look brave. ...You're not coming? Fine. Next time. I'll go easy. It's only a soup.
Hey, it's not that I can't cook! I just refuse to follow boring old recipes. Nothing ventured, nothing gained, right?
People around here need to be a little more experimental! When I was small the house always smelled like Sunday stew.
Clover barely remembers it. I'm trying to... never mind! Soup! Wait, what was I saying? Oh right, soup.
You're really nice to listen to me, you know that? Don't tell anyone I said so.
Festival prep is in full swing! I'm helping with the main dish this year, and I promise I'm sticking to the plan. Mostly.
Just don't tell Clover I'm practising on the neighbours!

variants: Tea? I always have a cup. Honey Lemon Tea, the way they make it back home. Not that I miss the place.
Honestly, the tea was the only decent thing they ever produced. Take your time, {player}.
Ah, my best customer! Admittedly, the only customer to look at my eyes instead of my feather. Are they really that captivating to you?
Need something? Want something? Or are you just here to admire the shopkeeper? I stock all three, though the last one is free.
Some people are so worried about what others think. I get it, trust me. But sometimes you just have to enjoy life as it comes.
Tom is such a sweet young man. And don't get me wrong, while I do like honey, he's sweeter than I can handle.
Maybe I should stop messing with him or else before he dies of embarrassment.
I told Maya she looked 'radiant in the firelight' yesterday. She told me it was sweat and coal dust, and just stared at me.
Strange girl.
Cyrus came in for paper. He's got a certain aura around him makes you want to talk to him for hours, despite him not saying much.
What a charming dude.
Ariane is a fascinating woman. Quiet, striking, and completely unbothered by the rest of the world.
Sometimes I feel like we're total opposites yet being around her just gives you peace
Zoe asked me to provide a grocery delivery service for the elders, but Walter definitely doesn't seem happy with that idea!
Sorry, Zoe, I don't want to get chewed out by the old man. Even if it's for you

lines: Found a spot for the hive yet, {player}? Somewhere with plenty of flowers nearby. You will thank me later.
Real honey is nothing like these artificial ones.
Good spot! Now give the bees a few days. They know their business better than we do.
Hm. I do not see many flowers around your hive. Bees need blossoms to make honey. Maybe you should plant it near some flowers instead.
Take it back with your pickaxe and move it next to the flowers. They will be much happier.
Honey every few days. I should have brought bees to this valley sooner.
Ah, the famous new farmer! Welcome to my humble shop, {player}. Everything on the shelf is imported, and priced accordingly.
I'm Jonas merchant, shopkeeper, tea enthusiast, and a man who refuses to live life without a little color.
I arrived only a few months before you, so we are both newcomers.
Tell you what, you stop by often, and I'll save my best smile for you. Take your time, browse, tell me what you need.
And if anyone in town tells you to take things too seriously, just ignore them. I certainly do.
It makes the evenings much more entertaining.
Hello again! Why I came here? You look like someone who appreciates a good story, {player}. Ahem, ahem.
People always ask me why a guy like me ends up running a quiet shop in the middle of nowhere. Truth is... it's a heavy tale.
I used to be a renowned tightrope walker in a traveling royal circus, best in the eastern provinces.
Then one stormy night, a jealous rival greased the wire with cheap lard.
I fell forty feet straight into a cart of prize-winning cabbages.
Shattered my pride, ruined my favorite boots, and forced me into early retirement. ...You didn't believe a word of that?
Damn, I thought I got you! My acting is usually so good no one can tell.
Half the fun of being a merchant is seeing what people will buy.
Ah, {player}, you caught me in a reflective mood. I was just thinking about my days as a disgraced opera singer.
My voice used to shatter crystal goblets from fifty paces until a tragic incident involving a stray duck and a high C ruined my vocal cords forever.
A heartbreaking loss for the arts, really. ...Wait. You're giving me that look. Right, right you already heard the tightrope story.
Look, if people are going to pry into where I came from, I might as well make the answers entertaining, shouldn't I?
Truth is, my real past is far less theatrical and considerably more boring. Besides, a little mystery is good for business.
Now, are you going to buy something, or just stand there dismantling my tragic mystique?
{player}! There you are. You look awful. I mean that fondly. Farming suits you. I came all this way to talk about something important.
Tea. Honey Lemon Tea is my favourite, I told you. But the imported artificial honey they sell here has no flavour at all.
Sweet and flat, like a polite compliance form. But I have seen the native flowers growing all over this valley.
Real honey could be made here! You have a farm. I have memories to chase. Take this hive, I made it from spare boards.
Put it on grass, with plenty of flowers within five tiles. And when you have the first honey, bring it to me.
I want to see if it tastes like home... or at least better than it.
Is that the honey? Let me see... Hm. Well it's darker than what we make back home. And the taste is sharper too But it is good!
Good in its own way. Keep some for yourself.
So you have greeted the whole village, {player}! Everyone here talks about you already. Here, a little welcome gift from the shop.
Carrot seeds. They grow fast, you will like them.
A festival! Back home, a celebration meant rows of stiff chairs and polite applause.
Here, they've got music, laughter, and mountains of cake. Honestly? It's a massive upgrade.
Your honey is going straight onto the feast table, I hear. Quite the honor! Try not to eat the whole jar before the big day, {player}.

variants: The old house is quiet today. Sometimes too quiet.
The ink dries faster than the thoughts can keep up... but perhaps that is for the best.
A quiet evening is a rare luxury. I find it leaves room for proper conversation, even if we simply share the silence.
I am glad our paths crossed today, {player}.
Do you ever feel like the air in this valley remembers things we've long forgotten? No? A foolish thought. Pay me no mind.
There is a distinct art to watching the world move without feeling the need to run with it. Most people never learn it.
Take a moment to breathe, {player}. The day will wait for you.
Watching Clover, you realize how separate her world is from ours.
This new generation sure is different from ours, perhaps it's a good thing.
Maya... I hope she is doing well. Ever since the divorce, every last responsibility fell squarely onto her shoulders.
Perhaps that is why she is always a bit all over the place.
Helen and Phil were polar opposites from the start I never truly understood why they married.
They must have thought their differences would complete one another. But in the end, all they found were arguments.
Every time I meet Martha, she doesn't stop asking about my health when she should be worrying about her own. She truly never changes.
And Walter that old fossil still insists he's as young and capable as ever.
I wish he'd just hand over the business to Tom and take care of himself for once.
Jonas? Who is that?
Hmm... the Briktens invited me for dinner. They aren't exactly a social family, so I do wonder who sent this. Definitely wasn't Walter.
Tom? He can barely meet my gaze when we speak, I can never tell if he's frightened or simply shy. Maybe both. Ariane? I doubt it.
She is straightforward; if she had something to say, she'd tell me directly.
When we were kids, she acted more like a mother to the rest of us than anything else.
Even now, it sometimes feels like she can see right through me. ...Wait. This handwriting? Oh, Zoe. I see what she did.
What a ball of positive energy she can't go a second without spreading it.
Well, I'm sure the Briktens won't mind me showing up uninvited.

lines: You're the newcomer we crossed paths the other day. If you're still finding your footing, I can offer a small piece of advice.
Harvest a crop and leave it in the shipping box beside your farm; it will pay out whatever you place inside.
Sell enough, and you'll have the coin to start properly.
I'm no authority on making money myself, a novelist rarely is, but one does what one can for a neighbour.
Ah... hello. You must be the new arrival. I'm Cyrus.
I write novels, mostly or at least, I let the ink flow until something resembles one.
Forgive me if I seem a bit distant; I was up rather late trying to untangle a stubborn chapter. I look after the old house by the mill.
It is far too large for one person, though all the papers keep it full enough.
If you ever need directions, a hand with something heavy, or simply a quiet place to sit, you're welcome to find me.
I hope the valley treats you kindly, {player}.
Good to see you again. Pay no mind if I looked lost, the waves of contradiction in my draft keep crashing over me.
My publisher tells me it isn't particularly cheerful, though I suppose it is through misery that one learns what true happiness actually is.
I do most of my writing at night... or so I believe. Sometimes it is rather hard to tell night from day anymore.
The town is quite peaceful today. How nice. I haven't left my room in a while, so this is rather refreshing... Care to take a walk?
The red flower on my chest? You like it? Thank you.
There was a time when people used to decorate the entire town with these, lining the fences, pinned to coats, woven into festival wreaths.
Slowly, year by year, the custom simply faded away. That is the nature of life, I suppose. Everything moves toward an end eventually.
Still... there is a quiet sort of dread in watching things vanish piece by piece, knowing that one day no one will even recall why they
mattered in the first place.
It makes you wonder how fleeting 'meaning' really is. Tell me, {player}... what do you think is scarier?
Living your life by carving heavy meaning into everything you encounter, or living a life where you see no meaning at all?
Ah, the festival. It is good to see the square so full of life, though I find I enjoy the celebration best from the quieter edges.
If you catch me lingering near the perimeter with a warm drink, feel free to come say hello.

variants: Why do plants need water? What's under the ground? Can I see?
Hi! I drew a duck. It looks like a potato. Maya says that's okay. Ducks are kind of potatoes.
Is it today yet? Is it tomorrow? How do you know which one it is?
Look, a snail! Hello, snail! He's not talking. Maybe he's shy. Like Tom.

lines: Hi! Who are you? Why are you here? What's that you're carrying? Is it a shovel? What's a shovel for? I'm Clover!
I'm not little, I'm medium. I live with my big sister Maya. She makes fire for a job. It's the coolest. I draw everything! Look!
This is the pond. This is a duck. That's a different duck. They're friends. Can I draw you? You've got a really interesting face.
No, a good one! The kind you want to draw twice. Do you know any stories? Not boring ones.
The ones where somebody goes somewhere they're not allowed!
Hi! Hi hi hi! Why is the sky that colour in the morning? Is it because it's tired? Maya says it's smoke. I drew your farm!
Here's the house, here's the fence, and here's you. You're the stick one holding a stick. Do plants get lonely?
What if you plant just one? Does it miss the others? I think I'd miss the others. Maya burned the soup again. I said it was good.
I lied a little. A little lie is okay when it's nice, right?
There are red flowers up the ridge! I saw them from the fence! They're so pretty, like tiny fires! But Walter says I can't go.
He always says that. Why? What's up there? Is it a dragon? Maya says it's just a hill. But when she says it she doesn't look at me.
That's what grown-ups do when they're hiding something. I know. Don't tell her I told you! I'm not going. I'm just looking.
Looking isn't going.
The festival! There will be games! And cake! Will there be cake? Maya says there will be cake but it won't be hers, I hope!
I want to wear a flower crown. A red one. Zoe says maybe.

variants: Hmph.
Hmph. You again.
...Hmph.
Weather's turning. Hmph. Good for the crops. Maybe.

lines: Hmph. A new farmer. Walter. That's my name. Don't wear it out. The old farm has good soil. Poor luck, though. People leave. You'll see.
Don't go up the ridge. Ever. I don't explain. Just don't.
Hmph. You again. My grandson says you seem decent. The boy likes everybody. It's a weakness. He works hard. Too hard.
Says yes to everything. Hmph. Tell him I said nothing. Go away.
See the fence round the old pen? I built that. Forty years ago. Still standing. Things last if you build them right. People too.
Some of them. ...Hmph. Why are you still here? Go. Plant something.
Hmph. Festival. Fuss and noise. In my day we did it properly. ...Fine. I'll sit at the front. Somebody has to.

variants: Have you eaten, dear?
Oh, hello, dear. Take your time. There's always a bench free.
Zoe's been fussing over you again, hasn't she? Let her. It's how she says she's fond.
Put your hat on, dear. The sun's sneakier than it looks.

lines: Oh, hello, dear! You must be the new farmer. I'm Martha, Zoe's granny. Come closer, my eyes aren't what they were. There!
Oh, you're taller than I thought. And thinner. You'll need feeding up. Do you eat enough? Nobody does, these days.
Zoe's been talking about you for days. 'The new farmer, the new farmer.' I told her, let the poor soul unpack first. She means well.
She plans everything. Even my afternoons. I'm an old woman and I have a schedule. Come and see us sometimes. There's always soup.
Always. Far too much of it, usually.
Dear! Sit a moment. No? Busy, busy. You young ones, always busy. I knit and watch the square.
You'd be amazed what you can see from a bench. Who's sweet on whom. Who's been crying. Zoe thinks I don't notice when she's tired.
I notice, dear. I always do. She talks and talks, our Zoe. It's her way of keeping the house warm. I let her. It does us both good.
Walter and I go way back. He's been a grump since he was young. A very handsome grump, if you can believe it.
He worries about the ridge. About the old stories. I tell him stories are only stories. But he's not wrong to worry.
Not about everything. Hm. Never mind. An old woman's chatter. Have you eaten? Take a moment. Don't argue, dear. It's only a bun.
Oh, dear, the whole village is helping this year! Zoe is running about like a little hen. Bring what she asks, dear.
A festival is only as good as its guests.
